text:
sophie: FYI customer reported sudden 429 bursts on their Private deployment behind their customer-managed gateway. They say it started after a traffic spike this morning and is persistent for a few minutes every hour. Full case id: CASE-2026-0445.

priya: ack. can you paste the gateway logs and ingress manifest? also want to know which ingress controller they run (nginx/traefik/envoy) and whether they preserve client IPs.

sophie: quick summary from customer: Private (VPC) deployment, redwood control plane private mode, customer-managed gateway running as a k8s DaemonSet -> envoy-based gateway in front of nginx-ingress. K8s ingress is nginx-ingress controller 1.5. They use token-based auth to the redwood private control plane.

sophie: logs from gateway around the incident (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-14T09:12:31Z] request id=abc123 upstream=redwood-inference svc status=200 latency=45ms
[2026-03-14T09:12:35Z] request id=abc125 upstream=redwood-inference status=429 reason=rate_limited
[2026-03-14T09:12:36Z] request id=abc126 upstream=redwood-inference status=429 reason=rate_limited
[2026-03-14T09:12:37Z] request id=abc127 upstream=redwood-inference status=502 reason=upstream_conn_failed
```

priya: ok 429s are being emitted at the gateway layer. two immediate suspects: 1) client IP not preserved so rate limiter collapses many clients into LB IP and hits token bucket; 2) double rate limiting between gateway envoy and nginx-ingress or the ingress-level limiters are misconfigured with too-small burst.

devon: can we repro from our lab? steps i use: spin up a small envoy gateway + nginx in a cluster, set service.externalTrafficPolicy: Local on the nginx service so ingress sees source IPs, then hammer with a quick stress script that preserves unique client IPs from multiple pods. repro script i use: 
```
# spawn 50 parallel curl workers from a k8s job
kubectl run curl-hammer --image=radial/busyboxplus:curl -i --restart=Never -- /bin/sh -c "for i in $(seq 1 1000); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} ' http://MY_GATEWAY/health; done" &
# or use xargs for concurrency
seq 1 200 | xargs -n1 -P50 -I{} curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://MY_GATEWAY/endpoint
```

matt: important note: nginx ingress annotations we commonly see: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps, nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-burst, nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections. If those are set low and envoy is also limiting, you'll get backpressure. Also check the envoy rate limit config. For envoy-based gateway we recommend a token-bucket with a reasonable burst of at least 50 for model-inference endpoints because clients can burst when apps cold-start.

sophie: customer provided their ingress annotations: 
```
metadata:
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "10"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-burst: "5"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: "20"
```

priya: yup that's small. 10 rps with burst 5 will cause 429s if a few clients spike. also check their Service spec. if externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster then source IPs will be the node IP and rate limiting by client IP is useless. ask customer to send 'kubectl get svc -o yaml' for the ingress service.

devon: also check redwood Private control plane quota config. we throttle per-tenant qps at the platform layer as well. the control plane will emit X-Redwood-RateLimit headers when it applies a quota. can you grep gateway logs for X-Redwood-RateLimit or rate_limit in headers?

sophie: grep snippet shows header present on a few 429 responses: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-redwood-ratelimit: tenant=acme,limit=60,window=60
x-redwood-retry-after: 10
```

matt: so that confirms platform quota was hit. two things to distinguish: is the quota being hit because of legitimate sustained qps, or because of misconfigured ingress/gateway that suddenly funnels many sources into one token bucket? ask customer for request distribution and if they saw a specific client doing retries.

priya: remediation suggestions for customer (order of operations):
1) Temporarily increase nginx annotations to a safer default: limit-rps: "200", limit-burst: "100". This is a quick mitigation to avoid too-frequent 429s while we debug.
2) Set service.externalTrafficPolicy: Local on the ingress Service to preserve source IPs if they rely on IP-based limits.
3) Inspect envoy gateway rate limit config and increase token bucket burst and refill rate. add metrics if missing.
4) Check client behaviors for retry storms. ensure exponential backoff and retry jitter on 429s.
5) If platform quota is legitimately tight, propose a short-term quota bump for the tenant while they tune upstream limits.

devon: commands i recommend collecting for triage: 
```
kubectl -n ingress get pods -o wide
kubectl -n ingress logs <gateway-pod> | grep rate_limit -n -B3 -A3
kubectl -n ingress get svc <ingress-service> -o yaml
kubectl -n ingress describe ingress <name>
# run gen load from k8s job to reproduce
kubectl run load --rm -i --tty --image=radial/busyboxplus:curl -- /bin/sh -c "seq 1 500 | xargs -n1 -P50 -I{} curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://MY_GATEWAY/endpoint"
```

gateway-bot: incident note recorded: CASE-2026-0445 linked to this thread. Suggested SLA impact: intermittent latency increase and 429s for small windows.

sophie: i've forwarded the mitigation steps to the customer and asked for the svc yaml + gateway envoy config. asked them to apply the temporary ingress annotation bump and report back in 30m.

priya: i'll prep a short runbook for recurring incidents: check for double rate limiting, preserve client IPs, align bursts between gateway and ingress, ensure platform quota matches expected peak qps. also recommend outbound guidance for customers on appropriate retries and jitter.

matt: note for internal follow-up: consider publishing a KB on 'Private deployments: common rate limiting pitfalls' covering exact nginx annotations, service.externalTrafficPolicy, and envoy rate-limit examples.

sophie: thanks everyone. i will update once customer confirms behavior after the temporary bump. :thumbsup:
